description: ecoinvent 3.13, released 2026-11-04, is registered and merged ahead of 3.12. Three things have to hold. First, the rows 3.13 re-registers -- the endosulfan isomers, propyl propionate and five organotins -- reach one substance from every ecoinvent release the build merges, because the earlier releases are corrected to the same numbers before matching rather than left to disagree (#26). Second, the seven corrections 3.13 ships itself -- Strontium II, Caesium I, the three lindane isomers, Molybdenum VI and the dinitrogen number on Nitrogen, organic bound -- still land where the corrected 3.12 rows land, now with no fix stated for 3.13. Third, the rows 3.13 retires and renames are accounted for. Measured against the five-list build of 5f06833, where all twenty-one endosulfan rows of 3.12 sat on one substance and 3.12's propyl propionate row was published as ethyl methyl carbonate.

expectations.title: Every ecoinvent `Alpha-endosulfan` row, from 3.12 and 3.13 alike, lands on the alpha isomer, 959-98-8
expectations.comment: On the build of 5f06833 the seven 3.12 rows landed on `Endosulfan`, 115-29-7, because 3.12 wrote the parent's number on them. 3.13 writes 959-98-8, and 3.11 and 3.12 are corrected to it, so the fourteen merged rows reach EF 3.1's alpha-endosulfan flows.

expectations.title: Every ecoinvent `Beta-endosulfan` row lands on the beta isomer, 33213-65-9
expectations.comment: The same measurement for the beta isomer: on 5f06833 all seven 3.12 rows sat on the parent.

expectations.title: The ecoinvent `Endosulfan` rows keep the parent's number, 115-29-7, and reach one substance
expectations.comment: Seven rows each in 3.12 and 3.13, one in 3.8. Nothing about them changes; this pins that separating the isomers did not move the parent.

expectations.title: The ecoinvent `Propyl propionate` row lands on propyl propionate, 106-36-5, from 3.12 and 3.13 alike
expectations.comment: On 5f06833 the one 3.12 row, b842b096, carried 623-53-0 -- ethyl methyl carbonate -- and was matched to EF 3.1's flow of that carbonate and published as `Ethyl Methyl Carbonate`. 3.13 registers the uuid 106-36-5 and 3.12 is corrected to match.

expectations.title: The ecoinvent `Dibutyltin` row reaches one substance under the cation's number, 14488-53-0, from every release
expectations.comment: One `water / ocean` row in 3.8, 3.12 and 3.13. On 5f06833 it was published under 1002-53-5, dibutylstannane, the neutral dihydride; 3.13 registers the dissolved cation and the earlier releases are corrected to it.

expectations.title: The ecoinvent `Triphenyltin` row reaches one substance under the cation's number, 668-34-8, from every release
expectations.comment: 3.8 ships 668-34-8, 3.12 shipped 892-20-6 (triphenylstannane) and is corrected, 3.13 ships 668-34-8 again. On 5f06833 the substance was published under 892-20-6.

expectations.title: The ecoinvent `Diphenyltin` rows of 3.8, 3.12 and 3.13 reach one substance
expectations.comment: 3.13 ships the row with no registry number and the formula `C12H10Sn+2`; 1011-95-6 is removed from the earlier releases so the three copies are placed by name alike.

expectations.title: The ecoinvent `Phenyltin` rows of 3.8, 3.12 and 3.13 reach one substance
expectations.comment: As for Diphenyltin: 2406-68-0 is removed from the earlier releases, following 3.13.

expectations.title: The ecoinvent `Trioctyltin` rows of 3.8, 3.12 and 3.13 reach one substance
expectations.comment: As for Diphenyltin: 869-59-0, trioctyltin hydride, is removed from the earlier releases, following 3.13.

expectations.title: ecoinvent 3.13's thirteen `Strontium II` rows reach `Strontium(2+)` with no correction stated
expectations.comment: 3.12 needed a fix from 7440-24-6, the metal, to 22537-39-9; 3.13 ships the ion's number, and its fixes file states nothing about the rows.

expectations.title: ecoinvent 3.13's five `Caesium I` rows reach `Caesium(1+)` with no correction stated
expectations.comment: 3.13 ships 18459-37-5, the number the 3.12 fix supplied.

expectations.title: ecoinvent 3.13's thirteen `Molybdenum VI` rows reach `Molybdenum(6+)` with no correction stated
expectations.comment: 3.13 ships 16065-87-5, the ion's number, which 3.10.1 to 3.12 had to be corrected to (#181).

expectations.title: ecoinvent 3.13's seven `Alpha-lindane` rows reach the alpha isomer, 319-84-6, with no correction stated
expectations.comment: 3.11 and 3.12 wrote gamma-lindane's 58-89-9 on the alpha, beta and delta rows and are corrected (#26); 3.13 writes each isomer's own number.

expectations.title: ecoinvent 3.13's five `Nitrogen, organic bound` rows reach `Nitrogen, Organic Bound`, not dinitrogen
expectations.comment: 3.13 ships the rows with no registry number, which is what the 3.12 fix did; it still writes the synonyms `dinitrogen` and `molecular nitrogen` on them, and the 3.13 fixes file still removes those (#57).

expectations.title: ecoinvent 3.13's two `Allyl alcohol` rows reach `Allyl Alcohol`, where 3.12's `2-Propen-1-ol` rows also sit
expectations.comment: 3.13 retires the seven `2-Propen-1-ol` rows, 107-18-6, and keeps the two `Allyl alcohol` rows under the same number with `2-Propen-1-ol` as a synonym. The merge already put both names on one substance.

expectations.title: ecoinvent 3.13's `Sodium stearyl fumarate` row creates its own substance, 4070-80-8, rather than landing on fumaric acid
expectations.comment: On the build of a87255f the row, which carries 4070-80-8, was matched by its vendor synonym `Fumaric acid` to EF 3.1's `fumaric acid`, 110-17-8, because no list carries the ester's number and the label matcher reads synonyms. The synonym is removed by the 3.13 fixes file.

expectations.title: ecoinvent 3.13's `Monostearyl fumarate` row creates its own substance, 1741-93-1, rather than landing on fumaric acid
expectations.comment: The same defect on the second ester, through the same synonym, measured on the same build.

expectations.title: The fumaric acid substance carries EF 3.1's thirteen rows and no ecoinvent 3.13 ester
expectations.comment: On the build of a87255f the substance carried fifteen flows: EF 3.1's thirteen and the two ester rows above.
